tldr: Meta had no dedicated AI coding-agent product until Aug 5, 2026, when it introduced Muse Code alongside an updated Muse Spark 1.2, framed explicitly as competition for Claude Code and Codex. CNBC's launch report and three other outlets covered the same framing through Aug 9, with no pricing, availability, or benchmark details disclosed for either product.
whats_new: Meta open-sourced Muse Glimmer on Aug 14 — a 30B-parameter, Apache 2.0-licensed model built for on-device agentic execution — the first concrete Muse-family spec disclosure since the still-unpriced Aug 5 Muse Code launch.
why_it_matters: Muse Glimmer gives platform engineers a real Apache-2.0 on-device agentic model to test for local/offline inference, while Muse Code — the direct Claude Code/Codex competitor — remains unbenchmarked and unavailable nine days after its launch.

status.detail: Muse Code and Muse Spark 1.2 still have no pricing, availability, or benchmarks nine days after their Aug 5 launch; Meta separately open-sourced Muse Glimmer, a 30B on-device agentic model, under Apache 2.0 on Aug 14.

beats.headline: Meta debuts Muse Code and Muse Spark 1.2, pitched against Claude Code and Codex
beats.summary: Persistent async background agents is the headline capability; the product is framed explicitly as a Claude Code/Codex rival from day one.

beats.headline: Comparison coverage continues four days later, no new specifics
beats.summary: Aug 9 pickup restates the same launch and comparison framing without pricing, availability, or benchmark updates.

beats.headline: Meta open-sources Muse Glimmer, a 30B on-device agentic model under Apache 2.0
beats.summary: First concrete Muse-family disclosure — parameter count and license — after nine days of undisclosed Muse Code/Spark specs; built for autonomous agents on consumer GPUs.

open_questions: Has Meta announced pricing or general availability for Muse Code and Muse Spark 1.2, separate from the now open-sourced Muse Glimmer?
Do independent benchmarks show how Muse Code's async background agents compare to Claude Code and Codex on real coding tasks?
Are Muse Glimmer's weights published on a hub like Hugging Face, and how does it benchmark against other open-weight on-device agentic models?
Is Muse Glimmer built on the same underlying model as Muse Code, or a separate model line?
take_for_builders: Muse Glimmer is the first Muse-family artifact you can actually pull and test — benchmark it on-device against your current local-agent stack; Muse Code still has no published specs to evaluate.
